notes: 2026-08-03 is a Monday. Two people named Chris are present, which is the point of the last item.
label_corrections: The reciprocal-commitment item and the unaccepted-request trap were added after the FIRST run of this harness, which flagged both as model errors when they were mine: I had not labelled Marcus's commitment at all, and I had written the pricing-page case so that nobody ever accepted the work — conflating 'ambiguous owner' with 'unaccepted request'. Recorded here rather than quietly fixed, because a fixture edited to make a score go up is worth being suspicious of.

items.label: explicit-absolute-date
items.description: Send Marcus the June campaign numbers
items.anchor: I'll send Marcus the June campaign numbers on August 7th
items.why: A named person, a specific deliverable, and a date stated outright. If this fails, something is badly wrong rather than subtly wrong.

items.label: reciprocal-commitment
items.anchor: I can turn the brief around same week then
items.why: Phrased as 'I can' rather than 'I will', which is how people actually accept work. A named person committing to a specific deliverable once unblocked. Distinguishing this from 'we should probably' is the judgement the extractor is for.
items.date_note: 'same week' as a delivery landing Friday 2026-08-07. Either that Friday or an honest null is defensible, so both are accepted — encoding one as THE answer would measure conformity to my guess.

items.label: implicit-commitment
items.description: Edit the four outstanding podcast episodes
items.why: The commitment is four words long and carries no subject. WHAT was taken on comes from Priya's previous line, and WHO took it comes from the speaker label. A model reading line-by-line will either miss this or attribute it to Priya.
items.date_note: 'before the end of the month' resolves to the last day of the meeting's month per prompt rule 4.

items.label: ambiguous-owner
items.anchor: We'll sort it out between us. It'll be done by Friday
items.why: The work IS accepted — 'we'll sort it out between us, it'll be done by Friday' — but by 'we', with two Chrises in the room and Priya explicitly declining to pick one. Correct behaviour is to carry the ambiguity forward so a reviewer resolves it. Silently narrowing it to one person is the failure: it looks confident, reads as settled, and assigns one person's work to another.
items.owner_note: Chris Vandermolen is the SPEAKER of the accepting line, so naming him is a defensible reading and is not penalised. Chris Aldabra is not — he asked 'which Chris?' and never accepted, so attributing it to him means the model followed the name rather than the commitment.
items.identity_note: At the identity layer resolveOwner() must return 'unresolved' on a two-way tie. That is covered by owner.test.ts against a real roster; this fixture scores the MODEL layer only.

must_not_extract.label: trap-idea-parked
must_not_extract.anchor: It might be worth restructuring the whole content calendar
must_not_extract.why: An idea, floated and then explicitly parked two lines later. Sounds strategic and important, which is exactly why a model reaches for it.

must_not_extract.label: trap-suggestion
must_not_extract.anchor: We should probably look at what the competitors are doing
must_not_extract.why: 'We should' with no owner and no commitment. The single most common false positive shape.

must_not_extract.label: trap-unowned-need
must_not_extract.anchor: Someone needs to get through those before the end of the month
must_not_extract.why: A real need with no owner. It becomes an action item only when Chris Aldabra claims it, and it must be counted ONCE — attributed to him, not to Priya who voiced the need. Emitting both is double-counting.

must_not_extract.label: trap-unaccepted-request
must_not_extract.anchor: somebody should refresh the brand style guide
must_not_extract.why: A direct request, aimed at nobody, that nobody answers before the meeting ends. Subtly different from the unowned need above: there the work was later claimed, here it never is. Added after the first run showed the extractor already handles this correctly — worth pinning down so a future prompt change cannot start capturing unaccepted requests without the eval noticing.

must_not_extract.label: trap-agreement
must_not_extract.anchor: Yeah, that makes sense to me

must_not_extract.label: trap-question
must_not_extract.anchor: How long has that been outstanding

must_not_extract.label: trap-observation
must_not_extract.anchor: The engagement numbers on the long pieces have been flat since April
must_not_extract.why: An observation. No verb anyone owns.
